name: Oscillator
description: Triangle-core oscillator: waveform morph, through-zero FM, hard sync and a sub octave.

name: Noise
description: White, pink, brown and blue noise. Colour sweeps from dark brown to bright violet.

name: Function
description: Rise/fall slope generator: LFO, envelope or slew, with four related outputs.

name: LFO
description: Low-frequency oscillator: classic waves, free or locked to the bars, with a fade-in.

name: Random
description: Seeded stepped randomness. Loop moves from always new to a locked loop.

name: ADSR
description: Attack, decay, sustain, release. Active stays high while the envelope runs: patch it into a Voice Cell's Voice Out.

name: Multi Filter
description: Stereo multimode filter: 25 virtual-analog algorithms (SVF, ladders, 1-poles, shelves, phasers, flanger), LP/BP/HP/notch mode, drive, key tracking, envelope out.

name: VCA
description: Stereo amplifier. Patch an envelope into Gain; Gain starts at 0 and goes up to 400 %.

name: Utility
description: The glue: attenuverter, offset, mixer, rectify/fold/quantize, S&H, slew, comparator.

name: CV to Notes
description: Pitch and gate in, notes out: lets a sequencer or any mono source play a Voice Cell.

name: Notes to CV
description: Notes in; pitch, gate, trigger, velocity and pressure out, with note priority and glide.

name: Attenuverter
description: Four rows of scale and offset; unpatched rows are manual constants.

name: CV Mixer
description: Four bipolar channels combined by sum, average, max, min or a scan across them.

name: Multiplier
description: Two four-quadrant multipliers: ring modulation, or one modulator scaling another.

name: Logic
description: AND, OR, XOR and friends for gates, plus a flip-flop and edge triggers.

name: Quantizer
description: Snaps a pitch or incoming notes to the notes of a scale: any modulator becomes a melody.

name: Switch
description: Sequential switch: 8 inputs to one output and one input to 8 outputs, stepped by triggers, the transport or Select.

name: Audio Mixer
description: Four stereo channels with level, pan, mute, solo and a send; return, master and limiter.

name: Crossfader
description: Blends two stereo signals with one knob, equal-power or linear.

name: Level Meter
description: Stereo peak and RMS meters with clip lights. The audio passes through; Level puts the loudness on a cable.

name: Dial
description: One big knob as a control signal, scaled to a range, smooth or in steps.

name: Button
description: A pad to press: gate while held (or toggled), triggers on press and release.

name: Keyboard
description: Play notes with the mouse or the computer keyboard. Notes out plays a Voice Cell.

name: Step Sequencer
description: Up to 32 steps of gate (with length), pitch, velocity and ratchet, quantized to a scale. Notes out plays a Voice Cell.

name: Drum Grid
description: 8 drum tracks × up to 32 steps (off, on, accent), 16 pattern slots, gate, accent and velocity out per track.

name: Ring Kick
description: Deep, round kick: a struck resonator that rings and dies away.

name: Ring Snare
description: Snare: two ringing drum heads and a burst of bright noise.

name: Ring Clap
description: Hand clap: a few quick bursts of noise and a short tail.

name: Ring Tom
description: Tom or hand drum: a ringing tone that falls in pitch, with a little noise.

name: Ring Rim
description: Rim shot or clave: short, high, woody clicks.

name: Ring Cowbell
description: Cowbell: two square waves through a band-pass, a sharp hit and a tail.

name: Ring Hats
description: Closed and open hi-hats from six detuned squares. Closed cuts open.

name: Ring Cymbal
description: Cymbal: a low clang and a long sizzle from six detuned squares.

name: Punch Kick
description: Hard, tight kick: a sine that sweeps down fast, with a noise click.

name: Punch Snare
description: Snare: two swept sines for the body and filtered noise for the wires.

name: Punch Clap
description: Bright hand clap: tight bursts of noise and a roomy tail.

name: Punch Tom
description: Tom: a sine that drops in pitch, with a touch of noise.

name: Punch Rim
description: Rim shot: a hard, bright crack.

name: Punch Hats
description: Bright, crunchy closed and open hi-hats. Closed cuts open.

name: Punch Cymbal
description: Crash or ride: bright, crunchy metal with a long decay.

name: Additive Osc
description: 64 sine partials shaped by tilt, odd/even, stretch, comb and chorus, or a drawn spectrum. Never aliases.

name: Arpeggiator
description: Plays the held notes one at a time in a pattern over up to four octaves. Notes out plays a Voice Cell.

name: Beat Oscillator
description: Two high carriers mixed down to their difference: a heterodyne tone that sweeps from kilohertz to a slow pulse. Pull makes them lock and stutter, Drift makes them wander.

name: Bender
description: Glitches by chance: repeats, re-pitches, reverses, slices and corrupts pieces of the input. Seeded by the song position, so a glitch you like comes back every time.

name: Bit Formula
description: Integer-expression sound generator: sixteen formulas plus your own, three modulatable knobs, a clock rate with pitch and an audio input in the maths.

name: Cartesian Seq
description: An 8 × 8 grid of notes walked by two playheads, or picked by X and Y. Notes out plays a Voice Cell.

name: Chart Recorder
description: A sprung pen draws the input onto a looping paper strip; the strip replays as modulation, at any speed or backwards.

name: Chord Osc
description: One pitch in, a whole chord out: up to six oscillators on a chromatic or diatonic chord, with inversion, voicing, latch, detune and stereo spread.

name: Chord Quantizer
description: One pitch in, a voiced chord out: four pitches and notes. Voice Leading picks the inversion that moves least.

name: Chorus
description: Stereo chorus (two swinging delay voices per side) or flanger (one, with feedback). Rate, depth, delay and feedback can all be modulated.

name: Clock Div
description: Eight clock dividers of one base clock, each output with its own division from /1 to /64.

name: Coin Toss
description: Sends each gate to A or B by a weighted, seeded coin. Two channels: independent, nested or opposed.

name: Compressor
description: Stereo compressor and limiter: soft knee, peak or RMS detector, sidechain input, parallel mix and a gain reduction output you can patch.

name: Crunch
description: Overdrive, bit crusher and sample-rate reducer in one, with a tone low-pass: from warm saturation to broken digital grit.

name: CV to Gate
description: Turns CV above a threshold into a gate, following the input or of a set length.

name: CV to MIDI
description: Four lanes that turn control signals into MIDI control changes (CC), 7 or 14 bit, sent only when the value moves.

name: Delay
description: A simple stereo delay: free or tempo-synced times for each side, feedback with low and high cut, and a ping-pong mode.

name: Delay Net
description: Up to eight delay lines feeding each other: scattered, jittered and reversed taps, a character in every feedback pass, and Parallel, Chain, Ring or Mesh routing.

name: Drum Map
description: Kick, snare and hats from a map of patterns: move X and Y to travel between rhythms, Density to thin or fill.

name: Drum Notes
description: General MIDI drum notes in; a trigger per drum out (kick, snare, rim, clap, hats, tom, cowbell, ride, crash) and the hit's velocity.

name: Dual Filter
description: Two morphing state-variable filters under one Cutoff, pulled apart by Spread: serial, parallel or stereo; formant pairs, wide band-passes, stereo filtering.

name: Dual Osc
description: Two analog cores with B → A FM, sync and a stereo wavefolder: a complete complex-oscillator voice.

name: Endless Tone
description: A tone that rises or falls for ever: octave-spaced partials under a spectral window, with rate, direction, width, count, timbre, stereo spread and a loop phase output.

name: Envelope Follower
description: Turns the loudness of audio, or the movement of a CV, into a smooth control signal with its own attack and release, plus a threshold gate.

name: EQ
description: Six-band parametric equaliser. Every band is a bell, low or high shelf, low or high cut, notch or band-pass. Frequency, gain and Q of every band can be modulated.

name: Filter Bank
description: Ten fixed band-pass filters: per-band levels, tilt, odd/even, a scanning window, band and envelope outputs, and a built-in vocoder via the sidechain.

name: Formant Osc
description: Pulse-formant oscillator: a resonant peak that sweeps through zero, vocal and filter-like with no filter.

name: Freq Shifter
description: Single-sideband frequency shifter: barber-pole phasing, bells and spirals with feedback, opposite shifts left/right, tempo sync, quadrature LFO out.

name: Gate Sequencer
description: Four tracks of 32 deep steps: probability, ratchets, nudge and conditions. Each track has its own length and rate.

name: Grains
description: Granular processor: records its input and plays it back as a seeded cloud of grains. Freeze holds the buffer; Feedback and Blur build endless textures.

name: Harmony Master
description: The board's key, scale and chord, from the knobs, a progression or played chords. Followers quantize to it.

name: Limiter
description: Brickwall stereo limiter: nothing passes the ceiling. Lookahead, release, input gain and a gain reduction output you can patch.

name: Low Pass Gate
description: Filter and VCA in one, opened by a modelled vactrol: fast to open, slow and darkening to close. Ping it for an organic pluck; Active frees a Voice Cell's voice.

name: Macro Osc
description: Sixteen synthesis models behind one Model knob and three macro knobs: analog pair, fold, FM, phase warp, grains, harmonics, wavetables, chords, vowels, noise, dust, string, modal, kick, snare, metal. Aux carries a second voice; Trigger strikes a built-in decay and low-pass gate.

name: Math
description: Two rows of arithmetic on signals: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, min, max.

name: Matrix Mixer
description: Up to 8 inputs × 8 outputs, a bipolar gain at every crosspoint. Snapshots store whole matrices; Morph blends two.

name: Meta Mod
description: Carrier meets modulator: one knob morphs through crossfade, fold, analog and digital ring, bitwise, comparator, vocoder and Chebyshev; an internal oscillator fills in for a missing input.

name: Modal Voice
description: Physical-modelling instrument: bow, breath, mallet or any audio drive a modal body (string, bar, plate, bell) in a small room. Active frees a Voice Cell's voice.

name: Monitor
description: Shows what is on a cable: a MIDI event table, an audio meter, a CV readout and a gate meter. Everything passes through.

name: Neuron
description: Two leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. In 1 is a bias, In 3 hears the other neuron: a rhythm out of the box.

name: Organic LFOs
description: Eight slow LFOs that move like a group of living things: related, never quite in step, the same on every render.

name: Patch Bay In
description: Collects signals into one bundle cable: every input you patch adds a channel, and a free one is always left.

name: Patch Bay Out
description: Splits a bundle cable back into its channels, named like the signals that go in at the other end.

name: Perc Voice
description: One percussion voice from kick to bell: Tone walks the partials from sine through membrane and bar to metal; FM, Modal and Noise Bank engines; Click, Sweep, Decay and Damp shape the hit.

name: Phaser
description: Stereo phaser: 2 to 12 swept allpass stages, feedback in both polarities, a stereo LFO offset. Mixed with the dry signal it makes moving notches.

name: Pitch Shifter
description: Shifts the pitch of audio by a musical interval, two crossfading delay heads, with drift for tape flutter and feedback for climbing spirals. Put it before a reverb for a shimmer.

name: Polymeter Seq
description: A step split into six tracks (trigger, note, octave, gate, probability, ratchet), each with its own length and division.

name: Pulse Generator
description: A lab pulse generator: exactly timed pulses with delay, width, slewed edges, bursts and double pulses. Its edges ring like a badly terminated cable: clicks, pings and small drums.

name: Quad LFO
description: Four LFOs: independent, in quadrature, spread in phase or divided from one rate. Free, synced or clocked.

name: Quantizer Suite
description: Four quantizers: scale with a note mask, transpose in the scale, arpeggiate, or follow a Harmony Master. Unpatched inputs take the previous channel's.

name: Recall
description: Random gates (T) and random voltages (X) on one clock. Recall repeats the recent past, up to a locked loop you can capture.

name: Resonator
description: A tuned resonant body that rings when something hits it: modal (string, bar, plate, bell), sympathetic strings or a plucked string. Feed it audio or strum it; up to four voices.

name: Verb
description: Stereo FDN reverb built to be played: every knob, Size and Decay included, modulates click-free; small rooms to endless pads, infinite decay and Freeze.

name: Rhythm Bank
description: Four related rhythms from a pattern number. Turn Pattern to browse grooves; modulate it to develop a part.

name: Room Print
description: Convolution reverb from a dropped WAV or ten built-in impulse responses, with predelay, stretch, trim, low/high damping and an early/late balance.

name: Rotating Div
description: Eight clock dividers of one base clock. Rotate shifts the set of divisions across the outputs.

name: Sampler
description: Polyphonic sample player and slicer: load a WAV, cut it into slices by hand, by transients or into beats, and play it from notes or triggers with up to 16 playheads, play modes, an envelope and a filter. It also records its audio inputs, to loop, overdub or use as a delay.

name: Saturator
description: Warm, organic saturation without the digital edge: tube, tape or diode curves, a frequency-dependent drive, power-supply sag and slow drift.

name: Segments
description: A chain of up to 8 ramp, step and hold segments: any envelope, or with a loop, an LFO of any shape.

name: Shape Env
description: Envelope and LFO that plays shapes from a library of 96, plus 8 you draw: one-shot, gated or looped.

name: Shape Table
description: A waveshaper whose transfer curve you draw: curve presets, drive, bias, edge behaviour (clip, fold, wrap), oversampling with antiderivative anti-aliasing and a harmonic read-out.

name: Shift Register
description: A looping register of bits. Lock moves from frozen through mutating to random; the outputs echo the pattern canon-like.

name: Six Slopes
description: Six slope generators with shared controls: Harmonics spreads their rates over overtone or undertone ratios.

name: Spatial Pan
description: A binaural panner built from synthesised cues: azimuth, distance and elevation with interaural time and level differences, head shadow, pinna notch, early reflections and Doppler.

name: Speak
description: A small formant speech synthesiser: a phoneme string sequenced at a rate, with vowels, nasals, fricatives and plosives, pitch, speed and formant shift.

name: Splice
description: Tape-style sampler and looper: record onto a reel, cut it into splices, play them at any speed and break them into windows, from micro-loops to clouds. Drop a WAV file on the reel to import it.

name: Stage Seq
description: Up to 16 stages, each a pitch held for 1–8 pulses with its own gate mode, slide and accent.

name: Strange Osc
description: An oscillator that is a chaotic system: four attractors at audio or control rate, a Tame knob toward periodic order, X/Y/Z outputs and a seeded start.

name: Swarm
description: A cloud of up to 16 oscillators spread over a chord or scale: blooms from unison into the chord, drifts, cross-modulates and fills the stereo field.

name: Sweep Generator
description: A function generator that glides from Start to Stop: risers, sirens, tone bursts, and a sweep ramp, pitch and marker triggers for gear that follows it.

name: Test Oscillator
description: A lamp-stabilised sine from a self-oscillating loop: it bounces, warms up and hums; below 100 % it rings when kicked.

name: Tidal
description: Slope oscillator from minute-long swells to audio rate: loop, AD or AR, with four related outputs.

name: Transport
description: Sets the tempo, switches Ableton Link on and off, sends and follows MIDI clock, and plays and stops the song. In the standalone app; elsewhere it shows the host's tempo.

name: Uncertainty
description: Six random generators: two fluctuating curves, two quantized steps, a shaped and correlated stored value and its integral.

name: Wave Analyzer
description: A very narrow tunable band-pass: pick single partials out of a sound, sweep them into a spectrum, or lock onto the strongest one and follow it.

name: Folder
description: Stereo six-stage wavefolder with tap crossfade, symmetry and an internal oscillator, anti-aliased for audio.

name: Wavetable Osc
description: 2-D wavetable oscillator: an 8 × 8 grid of band-limited cycles, paths, phase warps and your own WAV tables.

name: Wheel
description: A pitch or mod wheel as a control signal; springs back to the middle.

name: Wobble
description: One random stream in three shapes: Stepped jumps, Smooth glides, Wobble overshoots and rings.

name: XY Pad
description: Two control signals from one point on a pad.

name: XY Scope
description: An oscilloscope for X against Y: Lissajous figures that stand still when two oscillators lock, with Phase, Correlation, Ratio and a Still gate as outputs.

name: Zone Delay
description: Stereo delay from tuned combs to 20-second loops: five time zones, tape or crossfade time changes, loop characters, diffusion, Reverse, Hold and Ping-Pong.

name: MIDI In
description: Notes and controllers from a MIDI track (Bleep MIDI In).

name: Instrument
description: MIDI In and Audio Out in one plugin (Bleep Instrument).

name: MIDI Device
description: A connected MIDI controller: notes for Voice Cells, plus pitch, gate, velocity and CCs.

name: MIDI Out
description: Notes, CCs and pitch bend to another track (Bleep MIDI Out).

name: Audio In
description: The track's audio (Bleep Audio In).

name: Audio Out
description: Board audio to a track (Bleep Audio Out).

name: Audio Insert
description: A track's audio through the board and back (Bleep FX).

name: Audio Bridge
description: A Live track's audio through the standalone app and back (Bleep Audio Bridge).

name: Audio Return
description: The return of an Audio Insert (made by the compiler).

name: Link
description: Tempo, beat and bar from Ableton Link (or from Live through Bleep Audio Bridge).

name: Macros
description: The 16 automatable macros of the Bleep Board plugin.

name: Cell
description: A group of nodes with its own jacks. Double-click to enter.

name: Cell In
description: The cell's input: what you patch into this jack of the cell arrives here, inside.

name: Cell Out
description: The cell's output: what you patch into this jack leaves the cell through a jack of the same name.

name: Voice Cell
description: Patch one voice inside; the cell plays it once per note, up to 16 voices.
